claims.statement: \lean{split_exists_unique}\coined: every bilinear bracket is uniquely an antisymmetric part plus a symmetric part.

\lean{canonical_metric_bracket}\coined: on a real inner product space, a bilinear form $B$ that is symmetric (C1), degenerate along $u$ (C2: $B(u,\cdot)=0$) and invariant under every linear isometry fixing $u$ equals \[B(x,y)=c\,\ip{\Pi_u x,\Pi_u y}.\] The hypotheses do not mention $\Pi_u$. \lean{canonical_metric_bracket_sign}\coined: if $B(x,x)\le0$ then $c\le0$. \lean{Pi_u_form_symm_degen}\coined: the forced form satisfies C1, C2.

\lean{uniform_ceiling}\coined: if $M'\le CM^2-\kappa M^3$ and $\kappa>0$, then \begin{equation}M(t)\le\max\bigl(M(0),\max(C/\kappa,0)\bigr)\qquad(t\ge0).\end{equation} Also \lean{absorbing}, \lean{ceiling_antitone_kappa}, \lean{kappa_zero_no_ceiling}\coined{} (at $\kappa=0$, $1/(1-t)$ satisfies $M'\le M^2$ and blows up).

\lean{maxpoint_rate_logLoss}\coined: under \lean{EnergyIdentity}, \lean{StretchingLogLoss}, \lean{ViscousAtMax}, \lean{TetherFeedback}, \lean{CrossControlled}, \[y'\le\Bigl(C_1+\tfrac{\kappa}{4}+\tfrac{4C_2^2}{\kappa}\Bigr)y^2-\Bigl(\tfrac{\kappa}{4}-C_{\mathrm{abs}}\Bigr)y^3,\] so with \lean{uniform_ceiling} a uniform ceiling follows whenever $\kappa>4C_{\mathrm{abs}}$ (Young absorption at $\varepsilon=\kappa/4$).
\lean{scalarLaplacian_newtonPotential_eq}\coined: for $g\in C^2_c(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and $N(y)=1/|y|$, $\Delta(N\star g)(x)=-4\pi g(x)$ for every $x$.

\lean{newtonPotential_deriv_eq}\coined: for $h\in C^1_c$, $N\star\partial_jh=-\int G_j(t)\,h(x-t)\,dt$. (Regularized identity \lean{regNewton_conv_deriv}, then $\varepsilon\to0$ on both sides; the right side is dominated by $|t|^{-2}|h|$.)

\lean{biotSavart_eq_curl_newtonVec}\coined: for \lean{IsTestOrbit}~$\omega$, $\mathrm{BiotSavart}\,\omega=(4\pi)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}(N\star\omega)$ pointwise, $N\star\omega$ taken componentwise (\lean{newtonVec}).
claims.title: Step 5

claims.statement: \lean{curl_curl_newtonVec}\coined: for \lean{IsTestOrbit}~$\omega$, $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}(N\star\omega)=4\pi\omega$, using symmetry of second derivatives (\lean{fderiv_fderiv_swap}), $\operatorname{div}(N\star\omega)=N\star\operatorname{div}\omega=0$, and the step-3 theorem.
claims.title: Step 4

claims.statement: \lean{curlBiotSavartTest}\coined: \lean{CurlBiotSavartTest} holds, i.e.\ $\operatorname{curl}\mathrm{BiotSavart}\,\omega=\omega$ for every smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free $\omega$. Consequently \lean{helicity_casimir_test_closed}\coined: helicity is a Casimir of the Arnold bracket at such $\omega$, given the explicit argument $D\,S=u$.

\lean{biotSavart_selfAdjoint}\coined: for continuous compactly supported $a,b$, $\int\langle Ba,b\rangle=\int\langle Bb,a\rangle$ (Fubini with the majorant $|x-y|^{-2}|a(y)||b(x)|$, kernel symmetry, triple product).
\lean{helicity_gateaux}\coined: with $\mathcal H(\omega)=\int\langle B\omega,\omega\rangle$ (\lean{helicity}\coined), $2B\omega$ is a G\^ateaux representative of $\mathcal H$ on the test class.

\lean{curl_eq_of_isGateauxRepOn}\coined: two $C^1$ representatives of the same functional on the test class have equal curl. Hence \lean{helicity_casimir_of_rep}\coined: if $D\,S$ is any $C^1$ representative of $\mathcal H$, then $\operatorname{curl} D\,S=2\omega$ and $S$ is a Casimir of the Arnold bracket \lean{ArnoldBracketOf}; no hypothesis on the value of $D\,S$.

\lean{streamFunctionRepModGradOn_of_exists}\coined: \lean{StreamFunctionRepModGradOn} follows from one $C^2$ kinetic-energy representative $\psi$ with $\operatorname{curl}\psi=u$ and the Poincar\'e lemma \lean{CurlFreeIsGradient}\coined; the curl half of uniqueness is \lean{kineticEnergy_reps_curl_eq}\coined.
\lean{curlFreeIsGradient}\coined: every $C^2$ curl-free field on $\mathbb{R}^3$ is the gradient of a $C^2$ function.

\lean{decays_newtonPotential}\coined: if $g$ is continuous, compactly supported and $\int g=0$, then $|N\star g(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-2}$. Derivatives of $C^1_c$ functions and the coordinates of a divergence-free test field have mean zero (\lean{IsTestOrbit.integral_coord_eq_zero}\coined).

\lean{integral_pairing_curl_symm}\coined: \[\int\ip{a,\curl b}\dd x=\int\ip{\curl a,b}\dd x\]for fields with decaying coordinates and first derivatives. Hence, with $\psi=(4\pi)^{-1}N\star\omega$ (\lean{keStream}\coined), $\int\langle B\omega,B\varepsilon\rangle=\int\langle\psi,\varepsilon\rangle$, so $\psi$ is a $C^\infty$ G\^ateaux representative of the kinetic energy with $\operatorname{curl}\psi=u$ (\lean{keStream_isGateauxRep}\coined).
\lean{streamFunctionRepModGradOn}\coined: \lean{StreamFunctionRepModGradOn} holds unconditionally on the test class.

\lean{danskin_upper_dini}\coined: if $f,\partial_t f$ are jointly continuous on $\mathbb{R}\times K$, $K$ compact, then for some maximizer $x_\star$ of $f(t,\cdot)$ on $K$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, $\sup_K f(t+h)\le f(t,x_\star)+h(\partial_t f(t,x_\star)+\varepsilon)$ for small $h>0$; i.e.\ $D^+\sup_K f(t)\le\partial_t f(t,x_\star)$. \lean{vorticity_danskin_upper_dini}\coined\ applies it to $|\omega|^2$.

\lean{sup_mul_deriv_eq_inner}\coined: if $Y=\sup|\omega|$ is differentiable at $t$, then $YY'=\omega\cdot\partial_t\omega$ at every global maximizer. At such a point $\omega\cdot(v\cdot\nabla)\omega=0$ (\lean{inner_convective_eq_zero_of_max}\coined) and $\omega\cdot\Delta\omega\le0$ for $C^2$ fields (\lean{inner_laplacian_nonpos_of_max}\coined).

\lean{maxPointRealization_of_field}\coined: for a solution of \lean{ModelVorticityPDE} with $\nu\ge0$, $\omega(t)\in C^2_c$, $C^1$ in time, and $Y=\sup|\omega|>0$ differentiable, \lean{MaxPointRealization} holds with \lean{EnergyIdentity}, \lean{ViscousAtMax} and \lean{CrossControlled} discharged. The remaining hypotheses are \lean{FieldStretchingBound}\coined\ and \lean{FieldTetherFeedback}\coined. Running the ceiling argument from the one-sided Dini bound alone is open.

\lean{arnoldCasimirField_helicity}\coined: $2u$ satisfies \lean{ArnoldCasimirField}\coined\ ($\forall a$, \lean{ArnoldBracketOf} $\omega\,a\,(2u)=0$) on the test class. This is the clean form of \lean{EntropyCasimir} for the concrete bracket (\lean{entropyCasimir_of_arnoldCasimirField}\coined). The choice-based form \lean{EntropyCasimirChoice}\coined\ is kept and marked not provable as stated.

\lean{ceiling_of_upper_dini}\coined: if $M$ is continuous on $[0,\infty)$, $M(t+h)\le M(t)+h(R(t)+\varepsilon)$ for small $h>0$, and $R(t)<0$ whenever $M(t)>B$, then $M(0)\le B$ implies $M\le B$ on $[0,\infty)$.

\lean{field_uniform_ceiling}\coined: take a solution of \lean{ModelVorticityPDE} with $\nu\ge0$, $\kappa>0$, $C^2$ in space, $C^1$ in time, and support in a fixed compact set. Under \lean{FieldStretchingBound} and \lean{FieldTetherFeedback}, $\sup|\omega(t)|\le\max(\sup|\omega(0)|,C/\kappa,0)$ for all $t\ge0$. No differentiability of $\sup|\omega|$ is assumed; its continuity is proved (\lean{sup_continuous_of_uniform_support}\coined).

\lean{fieldTetherFeedback_cubicTether}\coined: for $T=-\kappa|\omega|^2\omega$ (\lean{cubicTether}\coined), \lean{FieldTetherFeedback} holds. Hence \lean{field_uniform_ceiling_cubicTether}\coined\ needs only \lean{FieldStretchingBound}. For a general tether it does not follow.

\lean{field_uniform_ceiling_logLoss_cubicTether}\coined: take a solution of \lean{ModelVorticityPDE} with the cubic tether, under the regularity and uniform-support hypotheses of \lean{field_uniform_ceiling}. Assume the named Prop \lean{FieldStretchingLogLoss}\coined, $\omega\cdot(\omega\cdot\nabla)u\le C_1Y^3+C_2Y^3\log(1+Y)$ at maxima. Then $\sup|\omega(t)|\le\mathrm{ceiling}(Y_0,\,C_1+\kappa/4+4C_2^2/\kappa,\,3\kappa/4)$ for every $\kappa>0$.
